candidates.buyer: Private employment/placement agencies (625 listed, 402 irregular) and the companies that must only use listed SPPs
candidates.existing: Competitor search (local language) found no DRC product. Only European temp-agency software (PilOTT, BeSTT, Recruit CRM) with no CNSS/ARSP logic. ONEM.cd and MIKUBA job portal (launched July 2026) handle job offers, not SPP compliance. Not found: any SPP reporting portal.
candidates.name: Compliance tracker for private placement services (SPP) and the companies that use them
candidates.trigger: Labour Code and the decree approving SPPs. Agrément, written contracts, medical cover, SMIG, CNSS/INPP/ONEM standing, IPP and quarterly reports. Moratorium April 2026, then closure of irregular SPPs. Enhanced control mission announced from February 2026. User firms face administrative and criminal penalties if they use unapproved SPPs.
candidates.unchecked: Quarterly report format, deadline and filing channel. Whether an agrément fee or renewal cycle exists. Whether the closed agencies leave enough paying buyers. Willingness to pay of a fragile, partly informal group. Whether the user-company side (large firms) is out of scope.

candidates.buyer: Congolese-owned subcontractors serving principal companies (mining, services, security, cleaning)
candidates.existing: The same SPP competitor search found no local software for ARSP declarations.
candidates.name: Subcontracting-law (Law 17/001) fee and registration tracker for Congolese subcontractors
candidates.trigger: Law 17/001 of Feb 2017 reserves private-sector subcontracting to Congolese-owned firms. The ARSP regulator collects fees on amounts invoiced to the principal company (percentage-based).
candidates.unchecked: Current ARSP enforcement and filing process. Scope uncertainty by sector. Fee rates and periodicity. Overlap with K03 (copper-belt subcontractors). Not verified from a primary source.

candidates.buyer: Bureaux de change (OHADA companies) and individual cambistes, plus financial messengers (messageries financières)
candidates.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
candidates.existing: Competitor search found none for DRC. Only a generic Tanzanian forex-bureau system (vvsdtz.com).
candidates.name: Record-keeping and regularisation tool for licensed cambistes and small bureaux de change
candidates.trigger: BCC Instruction administrative n°007 of 1 Sep 2023 on manual exchange. 20 Dec 2025: Force-Unie struck off; 50 messageries and 62 bureaux told to regularise with the direction de surveillance des intermédiaires financiers or lose their approval.
candidates.unchecked: Whether Instruction 007 requires registers, periodic reports or AML thresholds (the fetched page covers CEMAC, not DRC). Size of the licensed population. Willingness to pay. Whether BCC has its own reporting portal.

candidates.buyer: Artisanal mining cooperatives, comptoirs and negociants
candidates.existing: Not searched (budget). Likely dominated by state schemes (EGC, CEEC) and iTSCi/Better Mining, as in K07.
candidates.name: Cooperative and comptoir formalisation file for artisanal mining (ZEA allocation, 2026)
candidates.trigger: Ministerial orders of 3 April 2026 on allocating cooperatives in artisanal mining zones (ZEA). New commercialisation/export order separating sale from export. Artisanal copper-cobalt processing entities suspended from 19 Dec 2025, partly lifted Jan 2026. Certification and formalisation tools presented 6 Jul 2026.
candidates.unchecked: Competitor search not run. Whether cooperatives have a periodic reporting duty a small tool could serve. Rules vary by province. Field-operations dependency that killed K07 probably applies.

candidates.buyer: Moto-taxi owners and small taxi-bus owners in Kinshasa and provincial cities
candidates.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
candidates.name: Moto-taxi and minibus owner document tracker (plates, authorisations, insurance, vignette) under Kinshasa 2026 enforcement
candidates.trigger: Road-check operation from 26 Jan 2026 (licence, vignette, technical inspection, transport authorisation, insurance; fines, impoundment). Edict regulating moto-taxis voted 24 Apr 2026. Plate obligation since 2022.
candidates.unchecked: Promulgation and content of the moto-taxi edict. Whether owners are individual and tiny (low willingness to pay, mostly cash). Not checked: competitors.

candidates.buyer: Veterinary drug depots and agro-vet shops; vets under the new Ordre
candidates.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
candidates.name: Veterinary medicine seller and agro-vet licence compliance
candidates.trigger: Law 18/029 (Ordre national des médecins vétérinaires). ACOREP's claimed exclusive inspection authority (Matadi division installed Jan 2026) to clear clandestine outlets.
candidates.unchecked: Whether veterinary products fall under ACOREP or the livestock ministry. Existence of a vet-specific register or licence. Size of the market.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: No DRC-specific rule found on declaring domestic staff. Only the general Labour Code (Loi 015/2002) and INSS/CNSS contributions (commercial guide, unverified). Nothing new beyond general payroll.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No DRC scrap dealer licence or export rule surfaced; results were about Niger, South Africa, Senegal. Unverified for DRC.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Budget: no search spent.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Gold/mineral buying comptoirs and negociants sit under the Ministry of Mines/CEEC. A 2026 order separates sale from export, and artisanal cooperatives must be placed in ZEA zones (orders of 3 April 2026). This is close to rejected K07 and K03. See the cooperative-formalisation candidate.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Budget: no search spent.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Only old colonial-era ordinances found (1915, 1938, 74-241 on meat transport and trade), with current status unverified. No sanitary permit system or digital tool found.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Same as 6: nothing current found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Budget: no search spent.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Law 18/029 created the Ordre national des médecins vétérinaires. ACOREP claims exclusive pharmaceutical inspection across the country (Matadi division, Jan 2026). No vet-seller-specific licence rule or campaign found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: The search returned only French law. No DRC driller or abstraction rule found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Budget: no search spent.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Budget: no search spent.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Budget: no search spent.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: An IPPC-hosted Congolese decree on phytosanitary regulation exists (approval of products, import control, marketing), but I could not read the dealer rules. SENASEM/DPV roles unverified. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Strong lead. The Ministry of Employment and Labour audited 625 private placement services (SPP). 176 were compliant (Jan 2026), then 223 of 625 (Apr 2026), and 402 were irregular. They got a 30-day moratorium, followed by closure. Requirements: agrément, written contracts, medical cover, SMIG, CNSS/INPP/ONEM and IPP, quarterly reports. The subcontracting law 17/001 and ARSP fees are a second duty.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No DRC text found; results were Belgian, Swiss and French. Unverified.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: ASBL/NGO regime is Law 004/2001 (via a thesis), with provincial Justice divisions giving provisional authorisation. No annual-reporting rule or current campaign found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Kinshasa launched mass road checks on 26 Jan 2026 (licence, technical inspection, vignette, transport authorisation, insurance) and public transport shrank. A Kinshasa edict on moto-taxis was voted on 24 Apr 2026 (promulgation unverified). Moto-taxi plate costs USD 37 (2022). Heavy trucks of 20 t or more are limited to night circulation. Related to K05.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: BCC Instruction 007 (1 Sep 2023) governs manual exchange: bureaux de change (OHADA companies) and cambistes (individuals). On 20 Dec 2025 BCC struck off Force-Unie and told 50 financial messengers and 62 bureaux to regularise or lose their approval. Nothing found on market-trader tax platforms.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Nothing DRC-specific found for driving schools, nurseries or food producers. Unverified.
